ai-at-work.title: Upbound open-sources Modelplane to optimize inference clusters
ai-at-work.excerpt: Upbound Inc. today released Modelplane, a new open-source tool for managing artificial intelligence inference clusters. San Francisco-based Upbound is backed by $69 million from Alphabet Inc.’s GV fun
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Upbound released Modelplane, an open-source tool designed to manage AI inference clusters more efficiently, built on their existing Crossplane infrastructure management platform. For digital workplace leaders deploying AI tools across distributed teams, this means better control over the computational resources running those models without getting locked into vendor solutions. Whether this actually solves the real problem of getting AI infrastructure out of the hands of engineers and into something business teams can understand remains to be seen, but at least it's open source, which is a good sign.

ai-at-work.title: Nvidia bets on agentic AI to turbocharge biotech discovery
ai-at-work.excerpt: Artificial intelligence played a prominent role at this week’s Bio International Convention in San Diego, the largest biotech event with vendors spanning the full ecosystem of companies in this indust
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nvidia is pushing agentic AI, agents that can autonomously complete complex tasks, as the next big thing for biotech research and discovery. For digital workplace folks, this matters because autonomous AI agents will fundamentally change how knowledge work gets done, forcing us to rethink everything from workflows to skill requirements to oversight structures. That said, I'll believe it when I see enterprise adoption actually move beyond the hype cycle and solve real problems without requiring a team of prompt engineers babysitting the bots.

ai-at-work.title: Orderful nabs $35M to streamline supply chain data management
ai-at-work.excerpt: Orderful Inc., a startup using artificial intelligence to make supply chains more efficient, today announced that it has raised $35 million in funding. The Series C round was led by Koch Disruptive Te
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Orderful just scored $35 million in Series C funding to help retailers and suppliers swap data without losing their minds in the process. For digital workplace pros, this matters because supply chain chaos directly impacts internal systems, collaboration tools, and how your employees actually get work done when vendors can't send a clean PO to save their lives. Look, after 30 years I've seen plenty of startups promise to fix broken data flows, and some actually do it, so we'll see if Orderful is the real deal or just another well-funded band aid.

ai-at-work.title: Snyk launches Evo Agentic Development Security to police AI coding agents
ai-at-work.excerpt: Cybersecurity company Snyk Ltd. today launched Evo Agentic Development Security, a new layer of its artificial intelligence security platform built to police the autonomous coding agents that increasi
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Snyk built a new security layer called Evo ADS that watches over AI coding agents as they autonomously write enterprise software with minimal human involvement. This matters because enterprises are letting machines write code but nobody's really policing what those machines pull in or how they do it, which is a security nightmare waiting to happen. Finally someone's tackling the obvious problem: we've handed the keys to the robot, and now we need a security guard to watch the robot.

tools-tech.title: What do the IPOs for SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic mean for Microsoft?
tools-tech.excerpt: The AI IPO tsunami on the stock market has only recently gotten under way, with SpaceX’s more-than-$2 trillion IPO likely to be followed in several months by OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s IPOs — each of wh
tools-tech.dwp_take: SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are heading to IPO with valuations around $1-2 trillion each, creating direct competition for Microsoft in AI markets. This matters because it signals where enterprise AI investment is flowing and whether Microsoft's current AI partnerships actually lock in long-term advantage or just buy time. Honestly, if these three actually deliver on their hype at scale, Microsoft's "we own the AI future" narrative gets a lot harder to defend, and CIOs will finally have real alternatives instead of just Azure bundling.

tools-tech.title: Entry-level AI workers now need ‘senior-level’ skills, PwC says
tools-tech.excerpt: AI has created a tough job environment for entry-level workers and things aren’t getting better anytime soon — even those with AI capabilities now need “senior-level” skills to land a job. “AI-exposed
tools-tech.dwp_take: PwC's research shows that entry-level AI jobs now demand senior-level skills like judgment and leadership, making it seven times harder for newcomers to break in. This matters because digital workplace teams are struggling to build sustainable talent pipelines when there's no actual entry point anymore. It's the classic consulting move: create a problem, then charge clients six figures to hire expensive seniors to fix the shortage they helped create.

tools-tech.title: Trump vs. Anthropic: The AI wars are heating up
tools-tech.excerpt: The US government decision to force Anthropic to close down its latest and greatest AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, was only the next step in a burgeoning battle between AI providers and ignorant pol
tools-tech.dwp_take: The Trump administration has forced Anthropic to shut down its latest AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, escalating tensions between government regulators and AI companies. This matters because your enterprise is caught in the crossfire: if the government starts dictating which AI tools you can and cannot use, your digital workplace strategy gets a lot messier and less predictable. Here's the thing though: calling politicians "ignorant" doesn't help anybody, and neither does the breathless hype about AI being scary. We need actual guardrails, not theater.

tools-tech.title: ‘Agentic AI’ PCs? Not much new here, say analysts
tools-tech.excerpt: Nvidia and Microsoft this month touted the reinvention of computers with a new class of “agentic AI PCs” that will “reinvent the way PCs work.” That’s how Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described the compute
tools-tech.dwp_take: Nvidia and Microsoft are pushing "agentic AI PCs" as revolutionary machines that will fundamentally change how computers work, with Nvidia introducing its new N1X chip designed specifically for this purpose. This matters because if these systems actually deliver on autonomous task handling, they could reshape how knowledge workers interact with their tools, potentially reducing grunt work and changing job functions. That said, we've heard "revolutionary PC reinvention" pitches before, and until these agents actually do something useful without breaking your workflow, it's mostly marketing noise dressed up in silicon.

digital-culture.title: Liquid Death founder Mike Cessario shares his playbook for breaking through
digital-culture.excerpt: Hello and welcome to Modern CEO! I’m Stephanie Mehta, CEO and chief content officer of Mansueto Ventures. Each week this newsletter explores inclusive approaches to leadership drawn from conversations
digital-culture.dwp_take: Mike Cessario, founder of Liquid Death (the canned water brand with the skull logo), shared his leadership approach in Fast Company's Modern CEO newsletter, focusing on breaking through in a crowded market. Digital workplace leaders should care because his strategies around authentic branding and cutting through noise apply directly to internal communications and company culture. Here's the thing though: if your internal messaging needs a skull and edgy marketing to get employees engaged, you've probably got bigger problems than a branding issue.

industry-news.title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Glucose Monitoring Apps: The Good, the Bad, and the Limitations
industry-news.excerpt: Compare the best Samsung Watch CGM apps and Wear OS tools for blood sugar readings, including Dexcom G6, Gluroo, and xDrip+. The post Samsung Galaxy Watch Glucose Monitoring Apps: The Good, the Bad, a
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung Galaxy Watch now supports multiple continuous glucose monitoring apps, giving users real-time blood sugar data right on their wrist through options like Dexcom G6, Gluroo, and xDrip+. This matters because workplace wellness programs are getting serious about chronic disease management, and wearables that deliver clinical-grade health data during the workday can actually reduce absenteeism and boost productivity. That said, most of these apps still have accuracy gaps and battery drain issues that'll frustrate users faster than a failed Teams meeting, so don't expect them to replace actual medical devices anytime soon.

industry-news.title: Meta Invests $900M in Fintech Startup CRED, Taps Founder to Lead WhatsApp
industry-news.excerpt: Meta’s $900 million CRED investment puts fintech founder Kunal Shah in charge of WhatsApp as the app pushes deeper into commerce and payments. The post Meta Invests $900M in Fintech Startup CRED, Taps
industry-news.dwp_take: Meta just dropped 900 million dollars on fintech startup CRED and installed its founder, Kunal Shah, to run WhatsApp, signaling a serious pivot toward payments and commerce within the messaging platform. For digital workplace folks, this matters because WhatsApp is where billions of your users already live, and adding payment rails directly into that space could fundamentally reshape how internal communications and employee financial services work in global companies. Honestly, it's a smart play by Meta, though I'd be watching how this lands with regulators who are already skeptical of the company's ambitions in financial services.

industry-news.title: Oracle Cuts 21,000 Jobs as It Rebuilds Around AI
industry-news.excerpt: Oracle cut about 21,000 jobs in fiscal 2026 as it restructures around AI and cloud infrastructure, raising questions for enterprise buyers. The post Oracle Cuts 21,000 Jobs as It Rebuilds Around AI ap
industry-news.dwp_take: Oracle is laying off 21,000 employees while pivoting its business toward AI and cloud services, essentially betting the farm that this restructuring positions them better for the future. This matters because Oracle is a major enterprise software vendor that thousands of organizations rely on, so leadership upheaval and strategic shifts directly affect support quality, product roadmaps, and your vendor relationships. Here's the thing though: every tech company claims they're restructuring "around AI" these days, but Oracle's actually got real cloud and database chops, so this might actually stick unlike some of the performative pivots we've seen elsewhere.

industry-news.title: Apple’s iOS 27 Beta 2: New Siri, RCS, and Wallet Changes Arrive
industry-news.excerpt: iOS 27 beta 2 adds Write with Siri, RCS replies, Wallet updates, and Home fixes, giving IT teams more to test before launch. The post Apple’s iOS 27 Beta 2: New Siri, RCS, and Wallet Changes Arrive ap
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple released iOS 27 beta 2 with updates to Siri voice capabilities, RCS messaging support, Wallet features, and Home app improvements that IT teams need to test before public launch. This matters because every iOS update means your organization's mobile device management policies, security protocols, and user support workflows might need adjusting, and beta testing windows are where you catch compatibility issues before they become everyone's problem. The real question is whether your IT team has the bandwidth to actually test this stuff properly, or if you'll be like most places and just pray it doesn't break anything critical when it goes live.
